newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas sinks more on technicals.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas sinks more on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures continued to lose ground late Monday in moderate trade, still pressured by a wave of technical selling and liquidation after key support was breached early in the session, sources said.
At 1445 EDT, July tumbled 10.9 cents to $2.13 per million British thermal units, while August was 9.7 cents lower at $2.145. Other deferreds were down by 0.7 to 7.7 cents.

"Locals have been punching it to the downside, looking to kick more (sell) stops out, but the size hasn't been that big, and we could rebound off this," said one New York futures trader, adding spreads now favored some up front buying.
With fairly mild weather over much of the nation expected to last through the week, some expected cash and paper to stay on the defensive for a while.
But most agreed the prospects for hotter weather and better air conditioning demand later in the month should temper the bears.

Chart traders grew negative Friday after July's close below trendline support. They noted sell stops were hit early today after the spot month broke $2.18, with more liquidation triggered by the break of $2.16. Next support was seen in the $2.085-2.095 area, with further buying likely near $2.05. July resistance was seen first at $2.21, then at $2.25, $2.37-2.38 and the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing gas was quoted four cents lower Monday in the $2.14-2.19 area. Midcon pipes were off a couple of cents to $2.01-06. New York city gate gas was talked little changed in the mid-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 31,807 contracts traded at 1410 EDT.
On the KCBT, July skidded 10.4 cents to $2.00, while deferreds were steady to 7.5 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by one-half cent to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
